title: Quarterly strategy runway and experiment gates for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: Define a defensible, experiment-driven quarterly runway that ties Hosted API lineup changes to clear OKRs, capacity hedges, and rollback gates. Scope covers model deprecation/onboarding policy, canary sizing, surge hedges across Dedicated/Dynamic pools, and a lightweight experiment gate model for shipping model variants to Hosted customers. Deliverables: 1) A decision map for model additions/removals with quantitative thresholds; 2) Canary & rollback sizing playbook; 3) Experiment gate template & metrics checklist; 4) Capacity hedge playbook mapping to Dedicated tiers and burst policies. This ticket consolidates inputs from Research (model perf profiles), Eng (capacity telemetry), Console (route metrics), and Sales/CS (customer commitments) to produce a single quarterly runbook and a templated PRD for subsequent sprints.
acceptance_criteria: Decision map created and reviewed by PM, Eng, Research - includes threshold metrics for add/remove (latency P90, cost per 1k tokens, quality regression score)
Canary sizing guidance with concrete configuration examples (traffic %, duration, monitoring thresholds) and a defined rollback flow
Experiment gate template published in Confluence with required metrics hooks (latency, error %, token cost, quality drift) and a sign-off checklist
Capacity hedge table mapping demand tiers to Dedicated/Dynamic pool recommendations and estimated cost impact per 10% traffic increase
Runbook reviewed in cross-functional sync and accepted by Console, Runtime, and Growth stakeholders
milestones: 2026-03-05: Kickoff and intake of perf profiles and top-10 candidate models
2026-03-12: Draft decision map and initial capacity hedge table (internal review)
2026-03-20: Canary & experiment gate templates ready; engineering feedback incorporated
2026-03-30: Final runbook & PRD published to Confluence; stakeholder sign-off
2026-04-07: Handoff to squads with sprint-level tickets for rollout
decisions: Adopt three-tier experiment gates: fast A/B (<=1 week), staged canary (2-7 days), staged rollout (>7 days)
Model addition requires quality delta <1% regression on sentinel prompt set and latency P90 within 1.25x baseline unless mitigated by quantization/optics
Capacity hedges will favor Dedicated burst reservation over instantaneous autoscaling for planned launches >20% traffic increase
Runbook will include an explicit fallback matrix mapping model variants by cost/latency trade-offs
risks: Underestimated cost of hedges if traffic growth is correlated across multiple customers
Signal quality for experiment gates could be noisy for low-volume routes (false positives for regressions)
Operational overhead if canaries are too small to detect regressions but too large to be reversible quickly
Cross-team alignment risk: Console and Runtime may need minor SDK changes to expose metrics assumed in the gate checklist
